sections.title: リーディング・ライティング

items.q: The company plans to (　) its business into Asian markets next year.
items.ex: expand で「拡大する」。expand A into B で「AをBに広げる」。

items.q: Because of the heavy snow, the flight was (　) until the next morning.

items.q: The police are (　) the cause of the accident.

items.q: Mr. Brown was (　) to lend his car to his son, but he finally agreed.
items.ex: be reluctant to ～ で「～したがらない」。but finally agreed(でも最後は同意した)と対比になります。

items.q: The new manager (　) up with a great idea to increase sales.
items.ex: come up with ～ で「(考え)を思いつく」。

items.q: Children under 12 are (　) for a discount on train tickets.
items.ex: be eligible for ～ で「～の資格がある、～を受けられる」。

items.q: The volunteers worked hard to (　) to the success of the festival.
items.ex: contribute to ～ で「～に貢献する」。

items.q: Jenny had to (　) up with the noise from the construction site next door for months.
items.ex: put up with ～ で「～をがまんする」。

items.q: The museum will be (　) closed for repairs from June to August.
items.ex: 6月から8月まで(期間限定)なので temporarily(一時的に)。

items.q:
A: Did you accept the job offer?
B: No, I (　) it down because the office is too far from my home.
items.ex: turn down で「断る」。

items.q: The hotel can (　) up to 500 guests.
items.ex: accommodate で「収容する、宿泊させる」。

items.q: Anyone can join the club, (　) of age or experience.
items.ex: regardless of ～ で「～に関係なく」。

items.q: The singer's new album was a huge (　), selling over a million copies in its first week.
items.ex: a huge success で「大成功」。

items.q: I would rather walk home (　) take a crowded bus.
items.ex: would rather A than B で「BするよりむしろAしたい」。

items.q: (　) the bad weather, the soccer game was held as planned.
items.ex: Despite は前置詞なので後ろに名詞(the bad weather)。Although は後ろに文が必要です。

items.q: The scientist (　) the importance of protecting forests in her speech.

blocks.label: [A]
blocks.title: The Four-Day Workweek
blocks.body:
In recent years, some companies have been testing a four-day workweek. Employees work four days instead of five but receive the same pay. At first, many managers worried that their companies would ( 18 ). However, the results of several trials have been surprising.
In one large trial in the United Kingdom, most of the companies that took part said that their productivity stayed the same or even improved. Workers reported feeling less tired and less stressed. As a result, ( 19 ). Many companies decided to continue the four-day week after the trial ended.
Still, the system may not work for every type of business. Hospitals and stores, for example, need staff every day. ( 20 ), some experts suggest that each industry should find its own way to give workers more free time.

qs.ex: 働く日が減ると「仕事量が減る」と心配した、という流れです。However のあと「結果は意外だった」と続きます。

o: companies had to pay more money
qs.ex: 疲れやストレスが減った結果として「病欠が減った」が自然です。
「すべての業種に向くわけではない」→「そのため、業種ごとに方法を探すべき」という因果関係です。

blocks.label: [B]
blocks.title: Seeds for the Future
blocks.body:
On an island in Norway, near the North Pole, there is a building that holds seeds from almost every country in the world. It is called the Svalbard Global Seed Vault, and it opened in 2008. Its purpose is to ( 21 ) in case they are lost because of war, natural disasters, or disease.
The vault is built deep inside a mountain, and its location was chosen carefully. The area is very cold, so the seeds can be kept frozen even if the electricity stops. In addition, the vault is high above sea level, so it is ( 22 ) even if sea levels rise.
The vault has already proved useful. In 2015, researchers working with seeds from Syria, where a war had damaged an important seed bank, asked to ( 23 ). They used the seeds to start growing the plants again in other countries.

o: protect copies of the world's seeds
study the climate of the Arctic
qs.ex: 戦争や災害で失われたときのために「種の複製を守る」のが目的です。
海面より高い場所にあるので、海面が上がっても「浸水から安全」。

o: take back some of their seeds
qs.ex: 預けていた種を「引き出し」、他の国で再び育てました。

blocks.label: [A]
blocks.body:
From: Megan Hart
To: Kenji Sato
Date: October 2
Subject: Volunteer English tutors

Dear Kenji,
Thank you for your interest in becoming a volunteer tutor at the Westfield Community Center. As I mentioned on the phone, our program helps children who have recently moved to this country and are learning English as a second language. Most of them are between 8 and 12 years old.
Tutors meet with one child twice a week, on Mondays and Thursdays from 4 p.m. to 5 p.m. You don't need any teaching experience, but you do need to attend a two-hour training session before you start. The next session is on October 14. During the session, our staff will show you how to plan simple lessons using games and picture books.
Since you mentioned that you can speak Japanese, I think you might be a great match for a 9-year-old boy named Haruto, who arrived from Osaka last month. His parents told us that he is very shy and has been having trouble making friends. Please reply by October 10 to let me know if you can attend the training session.
Best regards,
Megan Hart
Program Coordinator

qs.q: What does the Westfield Community Center's program do?
o: It trains people to become English teachers.
It helps children who are learning English as a second language.
It teaches Japanese to local children.
It finds homes for families from other countries.
qs.ex: our program helps children who have recently moved to this country and are learning English とあります。

qs.q: Before Kenji starts tutoring, he must
qs.ex: you do need to attend a two-hour training session before you start とあります。

qs.q: Why does Megan think Kenji might be a good match for Haruto?
o: Kenji used to live in Osaka.
Kenji has a son the same age.
qs.ex: Since you mentioned that you can speak Japanese とあります。

blocks.label: [B]
blocks.title: White Lines in the Sky
blocks.body:
When you look up at the sky on a clear day, you may see long white lines behind airplanes. These lines are called contrails, which is short for "condensation trails." They are formed when hot, wet air from a plane's engines meets the extremely cold air high in the sky. The water vapor in the air quickly freezes into tiny ice crystals, which look like thin clouds.
Most contrails disappear within a few minutes. However, when the air is very humid, contrails can stay in the sky for hours. Sometimes they spread out and become large, thin clouds that are hard to tell apart from natural ones. Scientists have found that these long-lasting contrails can trap heat that would otherwise escape from the earth into space.
Because of this, some researchers believe that contrails may contribute to global warming as much as, or perhaps even more than, the carbon dioxide produced by burning jet fuel, at least in the short term. Since contrails are made of ice and not gas, their effect lasts only as long as they stay in the sky. This means that reducing them could quickly lower aviation's impact on the climate.
One way to do this is to avoid the areas of the sky where long-lasting contrails are likely to form. In a test carried out in 2023, an airline and a technology company used computer predictions to change the height at which some planes flew. As a result, the number of contrails from those flights fell by more than half. However, flying around these areas can sometimes require a little more fuel, so airlines must find a balance.

o: hot, wet air from engines meets very cold air.
pilots release water from the plane.
the sun heats the air behind planes.
qs.ex: hot, wet air from a plane's engines meets the extremely cold air とあります。

qs.q: What can happen when the air is very humid?
o: Contrails disappear within a few seconds.
Contrails can stay in the sky for hours.
qs.ex: when the air is very humid, contrails can stay in the sky for hours とあります。

qs.q: Why could reducing contrails quickly lower aviation's impact on the climate?
o: Their warming effect lasts only while they are in the sky.
Contrails produce more carbon dioxide than jet fuel.
Contrails are made of gas that lasts for years.
Planes would no longer need jet fuel.
qs.ex: 氷でできているので、空にある間しか影響がない → 減らせばすぐ効果が出ます。

qs.q: In the test carried out in 2023,
o: planes used a new kind of jet fuel.
pilots flew lower to save fuel.
some planes changed the height they flew at.
qs.ex: change the height at which some planes flew とあります。

qs.q: Which of the following statements is true?
o: Most contrails stay in the sky for several days.
Avoiding contrail areas may require more fuel.
Contrails are made of tiny drops of oil.
Scientists agree that contrails cool the earth.
qs.ex: flying around these areas can sometimes require a little more fuel とあります。

parts.prompt:
以下の英文を読んで、その内容を英語で要約し、解答欄に記入しなさい。
語数の目安は45語〜55語です。
parts.body:
In many cities around the world, bike-sharing systems have become common. Users can rent a bicycle with a smartphone app at one station and return it at another station anywhere in the city.
These systems have several advantages. People can travel short distances quickly without waiting for a bus or looking for a parking space. Cities also hope that if more people use bicycles instead of cars, there will be less traffic and air pollution. Moreover, riding a bike is good exercise.
However, bike-sharing systems also have problems. Some users leave bicycles on sidewalks, where they get in the way of people walking. In addition, many bikes are damaged or stolen, and repairing or replacing them costs the companies a lot of money.
rules: 解答は、英文要約の解答欄に書きなさい。なお、解答欄の外に書かれたものは採点されません。
要約の内容が英文から逸れていると判断された場合は、0点と採点されることがあります。英文をよく読んでから答えてください。
parts.model: Bike-sharing systems, which let people rent bikes with an app and return them at another station, are spreading in cities. They are convenient, may reduce traffic and pollution, and give people exercise. However, bikes left on sidewalks get in the way, and damaged or stolen bikes cost companies a lot.
checks: 第1段落(シェアサイクルとは何か)の内容が入っている
第2段落の利点(便利・渋滞や汚染の減少・運動)が入っている
第3段落の問題点(歩道への放置・破損や盗難の費用)が入っている
本文の表現を言いかえて短くまとめている(However などで対比)
語数が45〜55語になっている
parts.title: ライティング(英文要約)

parts.prompt:
以下のTOPICについて、あなたの意見とその理由を2つ書きなさい。
POINTSは理由を書く際の参考となる観点を示したものです。ただし、これら以外の観点から理由を書いてもかまいません。

TOPIC
Some people say that more companies should allow their employees to work from home. Do you agree with this opinion?

POINTS
・Commuting
・Communication
・Productivity
rules: 語数の目安は80語〜100語です。
理由は2つ書きましょう。
TOPICに示された問いに答えていない場合や、内容がTOPICからずれている場合は、0点と採点されることがあります。
parts.model: I agree that more companies should allow their employees to work from home. I have two reasons. First, employees can save time on commuting. Many workers in big cities spend more than an hour on crowded trains every day. If they work from home, they can use that time to rest or to spend with their families. Second, working from home can increase productivity. Without interruptions from coworkers, people can concentrate on their tasks more easily. For these reasons, I think working from home should become more common.
checks: 最初に賛成か反対かをはっきり書いている
理由を2つ書き、それぞれに具体的な説明がある
POINTSの観点(通勤・生産性など)を使っている
最後に結論をもう一度書いている
語数が80〜100語になっている
parts.title: ライティング(英作文)

lines: Hi, Rachel. Are you coming to the department dinner on Friday?
I'd love to, but my daughter has a piano recital that evening.
Oh, that's important. Maybe you could join us after the recital?
It ends at eight, so I think I'll just go home.
items.q: What will Rachel do on Friday evening?
items.ex: 娘のピアノの発表会があり、そのあとは家に帰るつもりです。

lines: Excuse me. I'm looking for a jacket for hiking.
This one is waterproof and very light. It's on sale for 120 dollars.
That's a little over my budget. Do you have anything cheaper?
This one is 90 dollars, but it's not waterproof.
Hmm. I'll take the first one. Staying dry is important.
items.q: Why does the woman choose the more expensive jacket?
items.ex: Staying dry is important.(ぬれないことが大事)と言っています。

lines: Honey, the car is making a strange noise again.
Didn't you take it to the garage last month?
Yes, but they said it was fine.
Then let's try a different garage this time. My friend recommended one near the station.
items.q: What will they probably do?
o: Ask the old garage to check it again.
Take the car to a different garage.
items.ex: let's try a different garage this time と言っています。

lines: Hello, this is Mary Lewis. I have an appointment with Dr. Hill at three today, but I'm stuck in traffic.
I see. Do you think you can be here by 3:30?
I'm not sure. Could I come tomorrow instead?
Let me check. Tomorrow at ten is open.
items.q: What will the woman do?
items.ex: 明日の10時に予約を変えました。

lines: Ms. Taylor, I'm having trouble with my history report.
I can't find enough information about my topic.
Why don't you choose a broader topic? Or you can ask the librarian for help.
I'll talk to the librarian first.
items.q: What will Jason do first?
items.ex: I'll talk to the librarian first. と言っています。

lines: Did you see the news? The city is going to build a new stadium near the river.
Yes. Some people are against it because they're worried about traffic.
I think it will bring more visitors and help local shops.
That's true, but the city will need to build more parking.
items.q: What is one reason some people are against the stadium?
items.ex: they're worried about traffic と言っています。

lines: Welcome to Sunrise Travel. How can I help you?
I'd like to book a tour to Hokkaido in February.
We have a four-day tour that includes a snow festival.
That sounds wonderful. Does it include flights?
Yes, flights and hotels are included.
items.q: What does the woman want to do?
items.ex: 2月の北海道ツアーを予約したいと言っています。

lines: Kevin, have you finished the presentation slides?
Almost. I just need to add the sales figures.
Can you send them to me by noon? The meeting is at two.
Sure. I'll send them by eleven thirty.
items.q: When will Kevin send the slides?
items.ex: I'll send them by eleven thirty. と言っています。

lines: Mom, can I go to the beach with Tom's family this weekend?
Where are you going to stay?
At their friend's house near the beach. We'll come back Sunday evening.
OK, but call me when you get there.
items.q: What does the mother ask the boy to do?
items.ex: call me when you get there(着いたら電話して)と言っています。

lines: Excuse me. I bought this blender last week, but it doesn't work.
I'm sorry about that. Do you have your receipt?
Would you like an exchange or a refund?
An exchange, please. I still need a blender.
items.q: What will the woman do?
items.ex: An exchange, please.(交換で)と言っています。

lines: I'm thinking of joining a gym, but they're so expensive.
Why don't you try running in the park? It's free.
I tried, but I get bored running alone.
Then join my running club. We meet every Saturday morning.
items.q: What does the woman suggest?
items.ex: Then join my running club. と提案しています。

lines: Dad, I want to study abroad in Canada next year.
That's a big decision. How will you pay for it?
I'm going to apply for a scholarship. I'll also work part-time this summer.
OK. Let's talk about it with your mother tonight.
items.q: How will the girl pay for studying abroad?
o: Her parents will pay for everything.
By getting a scholarship and working part-time.
By borrowing money from a bank.
Her school will pay for it.
items.ex: 奨学金に応募し、夏にアルバイトもすると言っています。

lines: Hi, I'd like to send this package to London by express mail.
It'll arrive in three days. That will be 45 dollars.
Hmm, that's expensive. How about regular mail?
That takes about two weeks and costs 18 dollars.
I'll use regular mail. It's not urgent.
items.q: Why does the man choose regular mail?
o: It is cheaper and he is not in a hurry.
items.ex: 安く、急ぎではない(It's not urgent)からです。

lines: Have you heard from Brian lately?
Yes. He got a job at an airline as a mechanic.
He says he's going to train for six months before he starts working on planes.
items.q: What will Brian do first?
items.ex: 飛行機の整備を始める前に6か月の訓練を受けます。

lines: Excuse me. Is there a pharmacy near here?
There's one in the shopping mall, but it closes at seven. It's seven thirty now.
Oh, no. Is there anywhere else?
The convenience store across the street sells some medicine.
items.q: Where will the man probably go?
items.ex: 薬局は閉まっているので、向かいのコンビニに行くと考えられます。

lines: Lisa started working at a bookstore last year. At first, she was nervous about talking to customers. However, her manager encouraged her to recommend books she liked. She made small cards with her comments and put them next to the books. Sales of those books increased, and now Lisa is in charge of the store's displays.
items.q: What happened after Lisa made the cards?
o: She started writing her own books.
items.ex: Sales of those books increased とあります。

lines: Thank you for flying with Pacific Air. We have started our descent into Vancouver. The local time is 9:45 a.m., and the temperature is 12 degrees Celsius. Passengers with connecting flights should go to the transfer desk after leaving the plane. Please make sure your seat belt is fastened.
items.q: What should passengers with connecting flights do?
items.ex: should go to the transfer desk after leaving the plane とあります。

lines: Sea otters are known for using tools. When they find shellfish, they lie on their backs in the water and use a stone to break the shells. Some sea otters even keep their favorite stone in a pocket of loose skin under their arm. This behavior helps them eat food that would otherwise be difficult to open.
items.q: Where do some sea otters keep their favorite stones?
o: In a pocket of skin under their arm.
items.ex: in a pocket of loose skin under their arm とあります。

lines: Daniel had always wanted to learn Spanish. Last year, he found an online program in which he could talk with students in Mexico. He helped them with English, and they helped him with Spanish. After a year, he visited Mexico and met his online friends in person.
items.q: How did Daniel learn Spanish?
o: By talking with students in Mexico online.
By taking classes at his university.
By living in Mexico for a year.
items.ex: メキシコの学生とオンラインで教え合いました。

lines: Welcome to the Riverside Art Museum. Our special exhibition of modern Japanese paintings is on the second floor. A free guided tour of the exhibition will start at 2 p.m. at the information desk. Please note that the museum will close at 5 p.m. today because of a special event.
items.q: What is special about today?
o: The exhibition is on the first floor.
items.ex: 特別なイベントのため今日は5時に閉館します。

lines: Kiwifruit originally came from China, where it was known as a kind of gooseberry. In the early 20th century, the plant was brought to New Zealand, and farmers there began growing it. When they started exporting the fruit, they gave it a new name, kiwifruit, after New Zealand's national bird, to make it more attractive to buyers in other countries.
items.q: Why was the fruit given the name "kiwifruit"?
o: It was first found in New Zealand.
To make it more attractive to buyers abroad.
items.ex: 外国の買い手に魅力的にするため、国鳥にちなんで名前を変えました。

lines: Megan works as a nurse at a hospital. Because she often works at night, she found it hard to sleep during the day. Her doctor advised her to make her bedroom completely dark and to avoid using her smartphone before going to bed. Now she sleeps much better.
items.q: What did the doctor advise Megan to do?
items.ex: make her bedroom completely dark とあります。

lines: Attention, passengers. Due to strong winds, the 10:30 ferry to Green Island has been canceled. The next ferry will leave at 1 p.m. if the weather improves. Passengers can get a refund at the ticket office or change their tickets to the afternoon ferry.
items.q: What can passengers do at the ticket office?
o: Get a refund or change their tickets.
items.ex: Passengers can get a refund ... or change their tickets とあります。

lines: Hiro is a university student who loves cooking. Last month, he started a small business selling homemade bento lunches to other students. He uses vegetables from a local farm, and his bentos have become very popular. He is now thinking of hiring a friend to help him.
items.q: What is Hiro thinking of doing?
o: Hiring a friend to help him.
items.ex: He is now thinking of hiring a friend to help him. とあります。

lines: Many people believe that goldfish have a memory of only a few seconds. However, scientists have shown that this is not true. In experiments, goldfish were trained to push a lever to get food, and they remembered how to do it for several months.
items.q: What did the experiments show?
o: Goldfish forget things in a few seconds.
Goldfish can remember things for months.
Goldfish do not need much food.
items.ex: they remembered how to do it for several months とあります。

lines: Good evening, shoppers. Today is the last day of our spring sale. All kitchen goods are 30 percent off, and if you spend more than 100 dollars, you will receive a free shopping bag. The store will close in thirty minutes.
items.q: What will people get if they spend more than 100 dollars?
items.ex: you will receive a free shopping bag とあります。

lines: Emma wanted to reduce the amount of plastic she used. First, she started bringing her own bag and water bottle. Then she began buying vegetables at a local market, where they are not wrapped in plastic. She says these changes were easier than she expected.
items.q: Why does Emma buy vegetables at a local market?
o: They are not wrapped in plastic.
The market is near her house.
items.ex: where they are not wrapped in plastic とあります。

lines: The Eiffel Tower in Paris was built for a world's fair in 1889. At first, many artists in Paris disliked it and called it ugly. The tower was supposed to be taken down after twenty years. However, it was kept because it was useful as a radio tower. Today, it is one of the most visited monuments in the world.
items.q: Why was the Eiffel Tower not taken down?
o: Artists asked the city to keep it.
It was useful as a radio tower.
It was too expensive to take down.
items.ex: it was kept because it was useful as a radio tower とあります。

lines: Last summer, Ken's family moved from Tokyo to a small town in the countryside. Ken was worried about making new friends. But on his first day at school, a classmate invited him to join the baseball team. Now Ken enjoys life in the countryside more than in the city.
items.q: What was Ken worried about?
items.ex: Ken was worried about making new friends. とあります。

lines: This is a message for all employees. The office elevator will be checked tomorrow from 9 a.m. to noon. During this time, please use the stairs. If you need to carry heavy items, please contact the building manager in advance.
items.q: What should employees do if they need to carry heavy items?
o: Leave the items on the first floor.
Contact the building manager in advance.
items.ex: please contact the building manager in advance とあります。
